evidence.claim: Note 4 reports product, license and CDMO sales exactly as above.
Management explicitly attributes 19.3% biopharmaceutical sales decline primarily to healthcare insurance policies, VBP and VAT policy adjustment.
Existing drugs encountered interim pressure from healthcare insurance payment reform and deepening centralized procurement, causing hospital-sales fluctuations.
No material acquisition or disposal of subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures during H1 2026.
Yisaipu remains a key commercialized product, with a marketing team; company explicitly describes VBP pricing pressure.
TPIAO and EPIAO descriptions give clinical indications, market leadership and future growth drivers, not actual H1 2026 per-product sales growth.
Mandi remains a current commercialized product; narrative describes leadership and future growth drivers rather than actual sales figures.
2025 product sales fell 10.3%, attributed to VBP price cuts and health insurance policies; not a new isolated H1 2026 phenomenon.
No material acquisitions or disposals of subsidiaries, associates or JVs in 2025 either.
Mandi spin-off was a proposed separate listing/distribution; this is not evidence Yisaipu was sold or H1 2026 sales excluded Mandi.

conclusions: No support in reviewed reports for attributing product-sales decline to sale of Yisaipu or a major disposal/perimeter change.
Ex-license revenue change is an analyst arithmetic comparison, not a company-reported organic/constant-currency growth metric; VAT effect was not quantified.
Total revenue growth of 3.9% and adjusted profit growth of 26.5% must not be described as growth of legacy pharmaceutical sales.
Per-product H1 sales and price-volume effects for TPIAO/EPIAO/Yisaipu not separately quantified in reviewed company report and August PR; do not invent precise actual trends.
Overseas product-sales growth of 43% in company August PR is a small-base overseas measure, not group product growth.
Competition is an industry risk; report evidence directly supports reimbursement, VBP price pressure and VAT, not a quantified competition attribution.
